answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor identities to plant electrophysiology. Nodes authenticate by measuring action potentials across living yarrow tissues inside a shielded haven. Probes on a sable carbon substrate record voltage spikes triggered by optical pulses. An attacker must cultivate discrete living plants per identity, incurring continuous biological and hardware costs. However, circadian dormancy alters tissue resistance, occasionally causing false rejections.
